![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/cac32ab36217820b63574e011488721bf57652fa63b4cbb7e5029fb54ce26243.png)

$$

$$

Since the total area under the graph equals $1,$ we can express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.16) & =1-P(Z<-1.16) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.16)\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/48adcb6bd3b0d12b9bc935b2414d615e0014d905b89a9f7d632306cd30f08580.png)

$$
\Phi(-1.16) =  0.1230.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.16) & =1-Φ(-1.16) \\  & =1-0.1230 \\  & =0.8770.\end{aligned}
$$

e-13268.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on a Bounded Interval
e-13268.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z\sim N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-0.48 <     Z <   1.18).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/f9011a3355b8261e153842a43be45e9bb07240d88421e37f7297a7d0f807e101.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z),$ 

$$
P(Z \leq z) = \Phi(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.48<Z<1.18) & =P(Z<1.18)-P(Z\le -0.48) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.18)-P(Z\le -0.48) \\  & =Φ(1.18)-Φ(-0.48)\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.48) & =0.3156 \\ Φ(1.18) & =0.8810\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.48<Z<1.18) & =Φ(1.18)-Φ(-0.48) \\  & =0.8810-0.3156 \\  & =0.5654.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
P(Z\le -0.93)=Φ(-0.93)=0.1762.
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z\ge 0.17).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/759e123d5c61321e78b085260a14d5ae98a54b724b82b06cdecc46ff28072b8b.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Since the total area under the graph equals $1,$ we can express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 0.17) & =1-P(Z<0.17) \\  & =1-Φ(0.17)\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/83ab5f91c5ee81eeb4c31b42558af5c46cb59d74603b30913ab80dadeafc3317.png)

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(0.17)=0.5675.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 0.17) & =1-Φ(0.17) \\  & =1-0.5675 \\  & =0.4325.\end{aligned}
$$
